                  </ns0:note> stalk <ns0:note n="p" place="bottom">Suppose this Seed should have its Harvest in no Whirlwind, it will end in loss and disappointment, as Seed that never springs up into a stalk, nor hath bud or ear; All your worship of, and dependance on I<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />dols, and forreign assistance, will at best be as seed that yields neither stalk nor bud.</ns0:note>: the bud shall yield no meal <ns0:note n="q" place="bottom">Or suppose it produced stalk and bud, yet 'twill be no profit, but all lost labour, for the bud shall be lank, shrivel'd and blasted, and never yield meal, so was the fruit <ns0:hi>Israel</ns0:hi> reaped, from <ns0:hi>Pul</ns0:hi> to <ns0:hi>Menahem,</ns0:hi> and from <ns0:hi>E<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />gypts</ns0:hi> assistance to <ns0:hi>Hoshea</ns0:hi> against <ns0:hi>Salmaneser.</ns0:hi>
                  </ns0:note>: if so be it yield the strangers <ns0:note n="r" place="bottom">Or if yet <ns0:hi>Meal</ns0:hi> be <ns0:gap reason="illegible" resp="#PDCC" extent="1 letter">
                        <ns0:desc>•</ns0:desc>
                     </ns0:gap>ound in the bud, <ns0:hi>Israel</ns0:hi> shall be never the better, Forreigners devour it, so did <ns0:hi>Pul</ns0:hi> and his, and <ns0:hi>Salmaneser</ns0:hi> and his <ns0:hi>Assyrians</ns0:hi> eat up all.</ns0:note> shall swallow it up.</ns0:p>
               <ns0:p n="8">8 Israel <ns0:note n="s" place="bottom">In the former verse the Prophet foretells the lost labour of such pains and seed as <ns0:hi>Ephraim</ns0:hi> bestowed: Now he addeth somewhat more dreadful, the Harvest is ruin and destruction to the seeds man, he is swallowed up, and this is the effect of the Whirlwind, <ns0:hi>ver.</ns0:hi> 7. ordinarily Whirlwinds scatter the fruit, but here's one swallows up both labour and labourer.</ns0:note> is swallowed up <ns0:note n="t" place="bottom">Very soon and irreparably, as a man that is swallowed alive by a mighty overgrown Shark.</ns0:note>:<ns0:g ref="char:punc">▪</ns0:g> now <ns0:note n="u" place="bottom">Ere long, within three or four years at most, as I noted on <ns0:hi>chap.</ns0:hi> 7. <ns0:hi>verse</ns0:hi> 11. <ns0:hi>let.</ns0:hi> o.</ns0:note> shall they be among the Gentiles <ns0:note n="x" place="bottom">Carri<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />ed out of their own Country by <ns0:hi>Salmaneser,</ns0:hi> and dispersed at the pleasure of the Conqueror into <ns0:hi>Chatah Habor, &c.</ns0:hi>
                  </ns0:note> as a vessel wherein <ns0:hi>is</ns0:hi> no pleasure <ns0:note n="y" place="bottom">As worthless and useless cast out of doors, or if of any use, yet in basest and most contemptible; so shall these Captives be among the Nations whom they must serv<ns0:gap reason="illegible" resp="#PDCC" extent="1 letter">
                        <ns0:desc>•</ns0:desc>
                     </ns0:gap> or <ns0:hi>Israel</ns0:hi> impoverisht by chargeable confederates, is now lookt upon with contempt by them all, and cast off.</ns0:note>.</ns0:p>
               <ns0:p n="9">9 For <ns0:note n="z" place="bottom">The Prophet gives now an account why <ns0:hi>Israel</ns0:hi> was so impo<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />verisht, and why they should be so severely punisht, why so punisht of God, and why so slighted by man.</ns0:note> they are gone up <ns0:note n="a" place="bottom">Either gone, <ns0:hi>i. e.</ns0:hi> have sent Embassadors with rich presents to purchase as<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />sistance from <ns0:hi>Assyria,</ns0:hi> or gone with their tribute to procure the continuance of the <ns0:hi>Assyrian</ns0:hi> confederacy and aids. This confi<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />dence and trust in <ns0:hi>Assyria</ns0:hi> was accompanied with a casting off their dependance on, and subjection to God, this their sin was very great, and their punishment shall as their sin, be very great. Others refer this going up, unto their going into Capti<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />vity into <ns0:hi>Assyria,</ns0:hi> and it surely may be a prediction of what shall be (if it be not a Narrative of what is) done.</ns0:note> to Assyria <ns0:note n="b" place="bottom">It was at that time a mighty Nation, whose Kings were very great, and yet more proud then great, as appears in <ns0:hi>Sennacheribs</ns0:hi> deportment toward God and Man: This Kingdom had now grown on through <ns0:hi>Pul, <ns0:gap reason="illegible" resp="#PDCC" extent="1 letter">
                           <ns0:desc>•</ns0:desc>
                        </ns0:gap>iglath Pileser, Salmaneser,</ns0:hi> and <ns0:hi>Sennacheribs</ns0:hi> Reigns, was a terrour to enemies, and the vain confidence of this fool<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />ish and sinful people, for which they are particularly threatned, and severely punished.</ns0:note>, a wild asse <ns0:note n="c" place="bottom">This is differently applyed by inter<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />preters, some refer it to the King of <ns0:hi>Assyria,</ns0:hi> who is fierce, swift and haughty as the wild Ass, and all for himself, thus the <ns0:hi>French</ns0:hi> interpret it: So it suits well, <ns0:hi>Israel</ns0:hi> thou wilt be disappointed in thy expectation from <ns0:hi>Ashur</ns0:hi> a wild Asse, who seeks himself only. Others do refer wild Asse to <ns0:hi>Israel,</ns0:hi> who wild, untamed, and burning in lust, (as is reported of the wild Asse) rangeth far and wide for lovers; seeks every where for aids and succours.</ns0:note> alone by himself <ns0:note n="d" place="bottom">Solitary, or in a Wilderness, where is no path or tract; this will well suit them in their Captivity, when they shall be left as in a Wilderness, and may, as perhaps many did, fly into more remote and desolate places, and ramble into uninhabited places, and there take rooting, and give being to Nations which are now known to us, though we know not whence they descend<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />ed. Or alone by himself, in a posture fit to become a prey to the Lyon of <ns0:hi>Assyria,</ns0:hi> so 'tis reported the Lions make a prey of the wild Asses in the Wilderness, so will <ns0:hi>Assyria</ns0:hi> make <ns0:hi>Israel</ns0:hi> a prey.</ns0:note>: Ephraim <ns0:note place="margin">
                     <ns0:gap reason="illegible" resp="#PDCC" extent="1 word">
                        <ns0:desc>〈◊〉</ns0:desc>
                     </ns0:gap> 30.6. <ns0:gap reason="illegible" resp="#PDCC" extent="1 letter">
                        <ns0:desc>•</ns0:desc>
                     </ns0:gap>zek. 16.33, <ns0:gap reason="illegible" resp="#PDCC" extent="2 letters">
                        <ns0:desc>••</ns0:desc>
                     </ns0:gap>.</ns0:note> hath hired <ns0:note place="margin">Heb. <ns0:gap reason="illegible" resp="#PDCC" extent="1 span">
                        <ns0:desc>〈…〉</ns0:desc>
                     </ns0:gap>.</ns0:note> lovers <ns0:note n="e" place="bottom">Hath dearly bought the Friendship of <ns0:hi>Assyria</ns0:hi> in <ns0:hi>Pul</ns0:hi> and <ns0:hi>Salmaneser</ns0:hi>'s time, and more dearly bought Friendship of <ns0:hi>Egypt</ns0:hi> in the time of <ns0:hi>So</ns0:hi> or <ns0:hi>Sabacon</ns0:hi> or <ns0:hi>Sevechus</ns0:hi>; for beside all the treasure they laid out on this, they parted with their God for it, and set him against <ns0:hi>Israel.</ns0:hi>
                  </ns0:note>.</ns0:p>
               <ns0:p n="10">10 Yea, though <ns0:note n="f" place="bottom">Or yea, because they think this the way to prevent their calamities, but it shall appear, this was the ready way to bring their calamities upon them, and for as much as they have hi<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />red the aid of the Nations to secure them against their God and his Judgments, therefore <ns0:hi>&c.</ns0:hi>
                  </ns0:note> they have hired among the nations, now <ns0:note n="*" place="margin">chap. 10.10<ns0:g ref="char:punc">▪</ns0:g>
                  </ns0:note> will I gather them <ns0:note n="g" place="bottom">Bring <ns0:hi>Israel</ns0:hi> together by a se<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />cret and unfailing train. I will, saith God, assemble and herd them together, that they may be taken and destroy'd together. Others say God will gather the Nations together against <ns0:hi>Israel.</ns0:hi>
                  </ns0:note>, and they shall <ns0:note n="‖" place="margin">Or, <ns0:hi>begin.</ns0:hi>
                  </ns0:note> sorrow a little <ns0:note n="h" place="bottom">For a while before their final Captivity, they shall complain and be grieved;</ns0:note> for the burden <ns0:note n="i" place="bottom">The Tribute laid on them</ns0:note> of the king of princes <ns0:note n="k" place="bottom">by the King and Princes <ns0:hi>i. e.</ns0:hi> of <ns0:hi>Israel,</ns0:hi> but better as we read it, 'tis King of <ns0:hi>Assyria,</ns0:hi> the great King who boasted of his Princes.</ns0:note>.</ns0:p>
               <ns0:p n="11">11 Because <ns0:note n="l" place="bottom">This refers to what follows.</ns0:note> Ephraim hath made many al<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />tars <ns0:note n="m" place="bottom">Multiplyed either to many Idols, every one having his Altar, or multiplyed Altars in se<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />veral places to the same Idol. They had many high places and Altars in all of them.</ns0:note> to sin <ns0:note n="n" place="bottom">Both as acting against the Law of God which required but one Altar, and also these Altars were to sin, in that they were for Sacrifices to be offered on them to Idols. These persons did not intend them for sin, but their good intention did not, could not change the thing, 'twas sin however they intended.</ns0:note>, altars <ns0:note n="o" place="bottom">Either those here erected, or those they shall find in <ns0:hi>Assyria,</ns0:hi> when they come Captives thither.</ns0:note> shall be unto him to sin <ns0:note n="p" place="bottom">Either because forced in captivity to worship <ns0:hi>Assyrian</ns0:hi> Idols, and to attend their Altars and Sacrifices, or else by a just and dreadful judgment from God, delivering them over to their wilful blindness, and Idolatrous heart, since they would never be reclaim'd, nor taken off from sinful multiplying Altars, let them follow their own hearts, and set up what they will, much like that, <ns0:hi>Revel.</ns0:hi> 22.11. Or else thus, Altars shall be the oc<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />casion of his greater guilt and punishment, his Altars, <ns0:hi>i. e.</ns0:hi> his idolatrous worship shall be that sin that ruins him.</ns0:note>.</ns0:p>
               <ns0:p n="12">12 I have written <ns0:note n="q" place="bottom">Some read it in the future, and by way of question, shall I write? but most read as we, in the perfect or past Tense, I have written, by <ns0:hi>Moses</ns0:hi> first, by other Prophets afterwards, the Law was given to them, as well as to the two Tribes.</ns0:note> to him the great things <ns0:note n="r" place="bottom">For their importance, weighty; for their excellency, precious; and for multitude of precepts, counsels and directions, sufficient; my Law had all this in it for their conduct in all Righteousness to<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />wards God and Man.</ns0:note> of my law, <ns0:hi>but</ns0:hi> they <ns0:note n="s" place="bottom">All these things I have written.</ns0:note> were counted as a strange thing <ns0:note n="t" place="bottom">
                     <ns0:hi>Is<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />rael</ns0:hi> looks on them as nothing to them, they are a distinct King<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />dom, and have a distinct establishment, their Lawes are now become unpracticable to us, and we have by the wisdom of our Governours, other Lawes establisht for our worship<ns0:g ref="char:punc">▪</ns0:g> let <ns0:hi>Iu<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />dah</ns0:hi> keep to theirs, we will keep to our Laws. After 200 years desuetude, would it not be madness to introduce <ns0:hi>Iudah</ns0:hi>'s Laws, and innovate all in <ns0:hi>Israel,</ns0:hi> thus they contemned the excellent things of Gods Law, as if they were nothing concern'd in them. And thus all their sins at last become incurable diseases, which nothing but utter destruction of the sinners can put an end unto.</ns0:note>.</ns0:p>
               <ns0:p n="13">13 <ns0:note n="‖" place="margin">Or, <ns0:hi>In the sa<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />crifices of mine offerings they</ns0:hi> &c.</ns0:note> They sacrifice <ns0:note n="u" place="bottom">Or as for Sacrifices, my gifts, so some taking the words absolute, and in apposition read them and perhaps they are plainer and closer connected with the former when so taken. I have written to them, and they count it a strange thing, and the sacrifices and gifts which they call mine, I tell you what I account them to be; as for sacrifices, which now they pretend to give me, it is flesh they sacrifice and eat it when they have done, and I account no more of it: they sacrifice that they may feast and fill themselves with Wine and Mirth, and what is that to me?</ns0:note> flesh <ns0:hi>for</ns0:hi> the sacrifices of mine offerings, and eat <ns0:hi>it; but</ns0:hi> the LORD ac<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />cepteth them not <ns0:note n="x" place="bottom">Neither owneth them as his, nor taketh any pleasure at all in them. These sacrifices shall never expiate their sins nor reconcile me to them, saith God; I think here is a Meiosis in these words, they may be a softer expression of Hatred and detestation, which God bears towards such.</ns0:note>: now will he remember their iniquity, and visit their sins <ns0:note n="y" place="bottom">In his just and hot displeasure, he will reckon with them, and by punishing them for all, make them know he re<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />members all their sins. Here remembering and visiting are the same, and include punishment.</ns0:note>: <ns0:note n="*" place="margin">chap. 9.3. and 11.5.</ns0:note> they shall re<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />turn to Egypt <ns0:note n="z" place="bottom">Either alluding to their Bondage in <ns0:hi>Egypt,</ns0:hi> so <ns0:hi>Assyria</ns0:hi> shall use them. Or else it is an upbraiding them, for and minding them of their perfidiousness to <ns0:hi>Salmaneser.</ns0:hi> They had been ever Covenant Breakers with God and Man, this last part of treachery God will punish. Or else they shall return to <ns0:hi>Egypt, i. e.</ns0:hi> many shall to save their lives fly from the <ns0:hi>Assyrian</ns0:hi> into <ns0:hi>Egypt,</ns0:hi> and there seek their safe<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />ty, and if they preserve their life there, the punishment of their sins shall follow them. Exile, with misery as bad as Captivity shall be their lot there. So <ns0:hi>chap.</ns0:hi> 9.6.</ns0:note>.</ns0:p>
               <ns0:p n="14">
                  <ns0:pb facs="tcp:64193:154" />14 For Israel <ns0:note n="a" place="bottom">The ten revolted Idolatrous Tribes.</ns0:note> hath forgotten <ns0:note n="b" place="bottom">The same with <ns0:hi>chap.</ns0:hi> 2.8. which see; or <ns0:hi>chap.</ns0:hi> 4.1. and 6. <ns0:hi>ver.</ns0:hi> Either re<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />members not at all, or 'tis without love, thankfulness and con<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />sideration what becomes him towards God.</ns0:note> his Maker <ns0:note n="c" place="bottom">Who made, who preserved, who advanced them and gave them all those privi<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />ledges wherein they excel other nations, who brought them out of <ns0:hi>Egypt, &c.</ns0:hi>
                  </ns0:note>, and buildeth temples <ns0:note n="d" place="bottom">The word will bear Palaces, or Towers. It is like their Idol-Temples were Magnificent that they might boast of them, and strong like towers that they might for need Garrison and Fortifie them, and trust in their strength in a day of War and trouble.</ns0:note>: and Judah hath multi<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />plied fenced cities <ns0:note n="e" place="bottom">On like designs and motives doth <ns0:hi>Iudah</ns0:hi> multiply strong holds fortifying against threatned Judgments, making flesh their arm whilest their heart (as at this time of <ns0:hi>Ahaz</ns0:hi> his Reign and Apostacy) did depart from the living God.</ns0:note>: but I will send a fire upon his cities <ns0:note n="f" place="bottom">Bring an enemy upon them that shall besiege them in their Cities, and burn them which was effected by <ns0:hi>Nebuchadnezzar</ns0:hi> and his Armies about 130 years after.</ns0:note>, and it shall devour the palaces <ns0:note n="g" place="bottom">The stately Palaces of their Princes and Nobles in their Cities, these shall be burnt too, <ns0:hi>Iudah</ns0:hi> hath imitated <ns0:hi>Israel,</ns0:hi> and made himself like to <ns0:hi>Israel</ns0:hi> in sin, and God will make them like in sufferings; the Fire which their sin hath kindled, shall consume both.</ns0:note> thereof.</ns0:p>
